newsitem.title: USA: N.Y. state files rental car bias suit.
newsitem.headline: N.Y. state files rental car bias suit.

text.p: New York authorities Wednesday accused a rental car company of denying rentals to minorities in high-crime neighborhoods.

Americar Rental System gave maps to employees that identified with red ink "no-rent" and "use caution" zones in the city of Syracuse, according to a federal discrimination lawsuit filed by Attorney General Dennis Vacco.

The zones were based on news reports of crimes, and the so-called red-lining was used to deny rentals to minorities from those areas, the lawsuit said. White people from those areas generally were granted rentals, it said.

"Despite Americar's claims that its rental policies were based on crime rates in particular neighborhoods, in reality they had more to do with potential customers' ethnic origin or the color of their skins," Vacco said.

In some cases, callers from "red-lined" areas were given rentals but subjected to heightened scrutiny such as needing a "flawless" driving record or meeting higher credit line requirements, Vacco said.

The suit also accuses the company of discriminating against the elderly with a policy of refusing to rent to anyone over 65 and anyone who "sounded old." The staff also was ordered to deny rentals to anyone with an Asian accent, the suit said.
Named in the lawsuit were North Syracuse, New York-based Americar Rental System, its parent company RAC Holding Inc. and its owner, Patrick Tucci.
